selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Reverts a VPlan test-driver facility. The revert removes metadata preservation during plain-CFG VPlan construction, the vplan-test pass registration, a configurable test-transform pipeline, and metadata-directed conversion of VPInstructions into widening or replication recipes.
Changed symbols: PlainCFGBuilder::createVPInstructionsForVPBB; VPlanTransforms::runTestTransforms; VPlanTransforms::widenFromMetadata; VPlanTestPass; VPlanTransforms::createPartialReductions; VPlanTransforms::handleMultiUseReductions
Behavioral change: Removes preservation of !vplan.widen and !vplan.replicate metadata when building VPInstructions in PlainCFGBuilder.; Removes the vplan-test pipeline entry and its semicolon-separated execution of selected VPlan transforms such as cse, simplify-recipes, remove-dead-recipes, licm, and optimize.; Removes widenFromMetadata, which inserted VPWidenRecipe or VPReplicateRecipe before a metadata-marked VPInstruction, replaced uses, and erased the original instruction.; The removed recipe insertion/replacement path was explicitly described as testing recipe-level transforms without full legality analysis; no retrieved hunk changes the normal LoopVectorize recipe-ordering path.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; VPRecipe insertion/replacement; No crash assertion artifact was available, and the retrieved hunks do not mention "Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe".
Reproducer link: The removed functionality is invoked through a vplan-test pass and metadata-marked test inputs.; There is no evidence that the reported Clang -O3 attachment uses vplan-test or !vplan.widen/!vplan.replicate metadata.
Pass or subsystem link: VPlan construction; VPlanTransforms; LoopVectorize test infrastructure
Causal explanation: The revert touches VPlan recipe construction mechanics, and the removed widenFromMetadata implementation did manipulate recipe placement with insertBefore. Nevertheless, that path was a dedicated metadata-driven test facility rather than the ordinary LoopVectorize construction pipeline. Removing it and its metadata plumbing has no evidence-backed connection to the reported phi-like recipe ordering assertion in a normal Clang -O3 compile.
Causal confidence: 0.07
Build risk: Removes the vplan-test pass registration from PassRegistry.def, so tests or users invoking that pipeline cease to parse or run.; Removes test-only LLVM_ABI_FOR_TEST APIs and associated StringMap/PostOrderIterator dependencies.; The normal LoopVectorize pass remains present in the retrieved hunks; the principal risk is loss of test infrastructure rather than a production-code build regression.

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Fix masked_cond expansion.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Fixes masked_cond expansion during VPlan conversion to concrete recipes by reversing the operands used to create a LogicalAnd VPInstruction. Corresponding LoopVectorize tests update expected vector select operands for predicated early-exit and multiple-exit loops.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::convertToConcreteRecipes; single_exit_in_conditional_block; three_early_exits; diamond_with_2_early_exits; four_exits_2x2_diamond
Behavioral change: Changes LogicalAnd construction from {VPI->getOperand(0), VPI->getMask()} to {VPI->getMask(), VPI->getOperand(0)} during masked_cond conversion.; Changes generated vector predication/select expansion for early-exit LoopVectorize tests: the mask produced by an earlier condition becomes the select condition, while the newly evaluated comparison becomes the selected true value.; Does not add, remove, move, or reorder VPRecipeBase objects in the retrieved hunk; the change is to operands of a newly created VPInstruction.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; LoopVectorize; masked_cond expansion; No retrieved hunk contains the reported "Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe" assertion or a SmallVector recipe-storage change.
Reproducer link: The changed tests cover predicated loops with single or multiple early exits.; The reported reproducer is an unavailable real-world Clang -O3 attachment, and no evidence connects it to masked_cond or predicated early exits.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlanTransforms::convertToConcreteRecipes; predicated early-exit vectorization
Causal explanation: This is a production VPlan change in the same vectorizer subsystem, so it is more relevant than a test-only commit. However, it corrects operand ordering for masked-condition expansion and the observable effect is changed select-mask semantics in predicated early-exit output. The reported failure concerns ordering of phi-like versus non-phi recipes during plan construction; the retrieved change neither changes recipe insertion order nor directly touches phi-like recipe handling. The causal connection is therefore indirect and weak.
Causal confidence: 0.18
Build risk: Production VPlan transformation behavior changes for masked conditional expansion.; Regression coverage updates span predicated-single-exit, predicated-multiple-exits, and interleaved early-exit vectorization tests.; Risk is concentrated in correctness and expected IR for predicated early-exit loops, not in build-system or API compatibility.

Summary: Adds target-specific LoopVectorize/VPlan printing tests under a new llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan hierarchy. The added tests exercise and check printed VPlans for fixed-order recurrences, reductions, reverse vectorization, tail folding, histogram vectorization, and widened calls; no retrieved hunk changes LoopVectorize or VPlan implementation code.
Changed symbols: first_order_recurrence; vector_reverse_i64; foo; safe_dep; simple_memset; simple_histogram; print_partial_reduction
Behavioral change: Adds regression checks for VPlan debug-print output and recipe sequence in several vectorization modes and targets.; The first_order_recurrence and reduction checks explicitly expect phi-like recipes, including EXPLICIT-VECTOR-LENGTH-BASED-IV-PHI, FIRST-ORDER-RECURRENCE-PHI, and WIDEN-REDUCTION-PHI, before subsequent non-phi recipes in vector.body.; No algorithm, recipe-storage implementation, VPRecipeBuilder logic, or LoopVectorize plan-construction behavior is changed in the retrieved hunks.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; phi-like recipe ordering is indirectly covered by ordered FileCheck expectations; No crash assertion artifact was available, and no retrieved implementation hunk contains the reported "Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe" diagnostic.
Reproducer link: The added tests run opt -passes=loop-vectorize with VPlan debug printing.; They are not the reported Clang -O3 crash-62b480.cpp reproducer.

behavioral_change: VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe::execute again filters contained struct return types with isVectorIntrinsicWithStructReturnOverloadAtField() before adding them to TysForDecl.
Overflow intrinsics are again expected to be widened into vector calls returning vector struct values, followed by extractvalue operations and vector stores.
The restored tests again expect LoopVectorize to construct vector-body and middle-block control flow for these overflow-intrinsic loops.

assertion_or_trace: VPlanRecipes
VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe::execute
WIDEN-INTRINSIC
No retrieved reference to phi-like recipe ordering, first-non-phi placement, or the reported assertion text.
reproducer: No retrieved hunk references crash-62b480.cpp or reproduces the reported -O3 crash.
The restored tests exercise vectorization of multi-result overflow intrinsics, including vector struct results and extractvalue users.
issue_link.explanation: Relanding overflow-intrinsic vectorization expands the set of VPlan recipe graphs, including multi-result widened intrinsic values and extract users, so it can indirectly increase exposure to VPlan invariants. However, the retrieved implementation hunk changes intrinsic overload declaration typing during execution and the shown tests concern widened intrinsic output; neither demonstrates a modification to VPlan recipe storage, phi-like classification, or recipe ordering. The connection to the reported assertion is therefore indirect.

build_risk: Changes VPlanRecipes.cpp and restores broad LoopVectorize overflow-intrinsic regression coverage.
Restored tests cover fixed-width and scalable-vector multi-result intrinsic output and cost-model diagnostics.
No build, test-run, or crash artifact is available.
Five diff hunks were omitted from the retrieved evidence.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This revert removes the recently enabled LoopVectorize coverage for overflow intrinsics and changes VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe execution to append every contained struct return type when constructing intrinsic declaration types, rather than filtering fields through isVectorIntrinsicWithStructReturnOverloadAtField(). The accompanying tests revert overflow-intrinsic loops to scalar/non-vectorized expectations and remove overflow-specific vectorization tests.

steps.subject: [VPlan] Fix masked_cond expansion.

evidence: Changes operand order for LogicalAnd during masked-condition lowering.
It does not insert, move, classify, or verify phi-like recipes and has only broad VPlan control-flow overlap.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This VPlan fix corrects masked_cond expansion by reversing the operands used to build a VPInstruction::LogicalAnd in convertToConcreteRecipes. The resulting generated vector selects change their condition/value relationship, and the expected outputs for predicated single-exit, multiple-exit, and interleaved early-exit LoopVectorize tests are updated accordingly.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::convertToConcreteRecipes; VPInstruction::LogicalAnd; single_exit_in_conditional_block; three_early_exits; diamond_with_2_early_exits; four_exits_2x2_diamond
Behavioral change: masked_cond expansion now creates LogicalAnd with the mask as operand 0 and the previous logical operand as operand 1.; The transformed vector IR changes which predicate is used as the select condition in predicated early-exit and conditional-block cases.; Regression expectations are updated for single-exit, multiple-exit, and interleaved early-exit vectorization.
Reproducer link: The changed tests cover predicated early exits and conditional blocks under LoopVectorize, which overlap generally with VPlan control-flow construction but do not check the reported 'Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe' assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPlanTransforms::convertToConcreteRecipes
Causal explanation: The commit directly changes VPlan lowering in a LoopVectorize path and could alter the shape or use-def relationships of recipes in predicated control-flow plans. Nevertheless, the visible change only swaps LogicalAnd operands during masked-condition expansion; it neither inserts nor repositions phi-like recipes, and no ordering-check or SmallVector-related code is present. It is therefore a subsystem-adjacent but weakly supported candidate.
Causal confidence: 0.18
Build risk: Updates several existing LoopVectorize FileCheck expectations for predicated exits and interleaving.; Changes generated predicate semantics, so incorrect operand ordering could produce miscompilation or test-output changes.; No build, test, or crash-artifact result was supplied.

behavioral_change: masked_cond expansion now creates LogicalAnd with the mask as operand 0 and the previous logical operand as operand 1.
The transformed vector IR changes which predicate is used as the select condition in predicated early-exit and conditional-block cases.
Regression expectations are updated for single-exit, multiple-exit, and interleaved early-exit vectorization.

reproducer: The changed tests cover predicated early exits and conditional blocks under LoopVectorize, which overlap generally with VPlan control-flow construction but do not check the reported 'Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe' assertion.
issue_link.explanation: The commit directly changes VPlan lowering in a LoopVectorize path and could alter the shape or use-def relationships of recipes in predicated control-flow plans. Nevertheless, the visible change only swaps LogicalAnd operands during masked-condition expansion; it neither inserts nor repositions phi-like recipes, and no ordering-check or SmallVector-related code is present. It is therefore a subsystem-adjacent but weakly supported candidate.

build_risk: Updates several existing LoopVectorize FileCheck expectations for predicated exits and interleaving.
Changes generated predicate semantics, so incorrect operand ordering could produce miscompilation or test-output changes.
No build, test, or crash-artifact result was supplied.

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Use target's index type for {First,Last}ActiveLane instead of i64 (#186361)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This VPlan change makes FirstActiveLane and LastActiveLane-related values use the target index type rather than hard-coded i64. It initializes VPTypeAnalysis with the plan DataLayout, uses inferred scalar types for active-lane constants and casts, and adds RV32/RV64 LoopVectorize coverage for live-out and early-exit active-lane handling.
Changed symbols: VPTypeAnalysis::VPTypeAnalysis; VPInstruction::generate; VPlanTransforms::adjustFixedOrderRecurrences; VPlanTransforms::convertToConcreteRecipes; VPlanTransforms::optimizeMaskToEVL; VPTypeAnalysis
Behavioral change: Active-lane operations and their associated zero/one constants are typed from VPTypeAnalysis inference instead of being unconditionally i64.; The mask-to-EVL path uses createScalarZExtOrTrunc with the operand's inferred scalar type rather than always emitting a zext.; VPTypeAnalysis now retains the VPlan DataLayout, enabling target-index-type-sensitive type inference.; Generated code for FirstActiveLane and LastActiveLane differs between RV64 and RV32, with RV32 using i32 lane indices.
Reproducer link: The added tests exercise LoopVectorize early exits and live-out handling, which are VPlan plan-construction scenarios, but they do not reproduce or check the reported phi-like-recipe ordering assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPTypeAnalysis; VPlanTransforms
Causal explanation: The commit touches high-risk VPlan construction and transformation code, including recipe generation and active-lane handling. However, the retrieved changes are type-correctness changes for target index widths and casts; they do not visibly add, move, classify, or reorder phi-like recipes or SmallVector recipe storage. With the assertion artifact unavailable and no direct phi-ordering contact in the hunks, the causal link is weak and indirect.
Causal confidence: 0.15
Build risk: Adds target-specific LoopVectorize regression coverage for RV32, RV64, and ZVE32X.; Changes shared VPlan type inference and scalar-cast construction, which can affect generated IR across targets.; No build, test, or crash-artifact result was supplied.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change updates VPlanTransforms::narrowInterleaveGroups so that a narrowed loop step is also used to materialize the vector trip count, then replaces VFxUF uses with that step. It explicitly obtains the vector preheader and inserts the new multiplication at its beginning, restricts the transform to plans with a normal two-successor middle block or a scalar-epilogue middle block, and changes materializeVectorTripCount to insert after a defined Step recipe so def-use ordering remains valid. The patch adds regression coverage for previously crashing interleave-group/epilogue-vectorization cases involving a preheader PHI.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::narrowInterleaveGroups; VPlanTransforms::materializeVectorTripCount; LoopVectorizationPlanner::executePlan; VPlan::getVFxUF
Behavioral change: narrowInterleaveGroups computes a narrowed step, materializes the vector trip count using that step, updates the induction increment, and replaces uses of VFxUF with the narrowed step.; The narrowing transform now bails out unless the middle block has the expected two-successor form or a single successor to the scalar preheader.; Vector-trip-count materialization inserts after Step's defining recipe when Step is defined in the vector preheader, explicitly preserving def-use order.; LoopVectorizationPlanner::executePlan passes the plan VFxUF value into the relevant execution path.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; recipe insertion ordering; explicit valid def-use ordering preservation; preheader PHI
Reproducer link: A newly added test states that LoopVectorize must not crash when connecting an epilogue vector loop for an interleave group with a preheader PHI.; That test exercises a crash-adjacent VPlan/LoopVectorize configuration, but it does not show the pr193164 source or the exact 'Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe' assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlanTransforms; interleave-group narrowing; epilogue vectorization
Causal explanation: The change directly modifies VPlan recipe insertion in the vector preheader and explicitly addresses ordering validity, making it relevant to an assertion about recipe ordering. Its new no-crash test also involves a preheader PHI and epilogue-vector-loop construction. Still, the stated invariant is def-use ordering, not the required phi-like-before-non-phi ordering, and the visible code does not establish that the reported reproducer takes narrowInterleaveGroups.
Causal confidence: 0.49
Build risk: Adds substantial LoopVectorize regression coverage, including a test explicitly described as preventing a crash.; Changes VPlan insertion-point assumptions with an assertion that Step must be defined in the vector preheader.; No build, test execution, or pr193164 crash-reproduction result is supplied.

steps.subject: [VPlan] Optimize FindLast of (binop %IV, live-in) by sinking. (#183911)

evidence: Mutates VPlan recipes around a phi-backed find-last reduction and inserts replacement select recipes.
The transform is narrowly limited to sinkable find-last IV expressions and has no direct ordering-check match.

features: meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Vectorize, path:llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize, phi-backed-reduction, recipe-rewriting, term:computereductionresultnowconsumesfindlastselectandclonebinopforscalarivrecreatesthesunkbinaryoperationafterreductionforscalarexithandling.
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This extends VPlanTransforms::optimizeFindIVReductions to recognize a find-last expression formed from a widened IV and a live-in value, track the underlying IV through the reduction, create a replacement select in the loop block, and sink/recreate the scalar binary expression after the vector reduction. It changes the reduction input from the prior reduction result operand to the possibly rewritten FindLastSelect and updates epilogue find-last tests accordingly.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::optimizeFindIVReductions
Behavioral change: The transform uses getExpressionIV to identify a sinkable expression of a widened IV and computes SCEV from that underlying IV when present.; When such an expression is found, it creates a replacement select that tracks the underlying IV directly and rewires the backedge value used by the find-last reduction.; ComputeReductionResult now consumes FindLastSelect, and cloneBinOpForScalarIV recreates the sunk binary operation after reduction for scalar exit handling.; The exit select and ComputeAnyOfResult use VectorRegionExitingVal rather than ReducedIV, preserving the reconstructed expression at vector-region exit.
Assertion or trace link: The added assertion checks an SCEV/AddRec consistency condition and is not the reported "Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe" assertion.; The new code explicitly manipulates a select involving PhiR and inserts it with VPBuilder at the original select recipe, so it operates near phi-related VPlan recipe construction.; The crash-signal artifact is unavailable and reachability was marked text-unreachable.
Reproducer link: The added and updated tests cover find-last IV expressions, including epilogue-vectorization output.; No retrieved test or hunk identifies crash-62b480.cpp, nor establishes that its loop has the find-last reduction pattern required by optimizeFindIVReductions.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlanTransforms; VPlan find-last IV reduction optimization; Epilogue vectorization
Causal explanation: The commit is relevant because it mutates VPlan recipes around a phi-backed find-last select and adds recipes through VPBuilder, which could expose ordering-sensitive VPlan invariants. However, its scope is narrow: it requires a recognized find-last IV reduction with a sinkable binary expression. The retrieved evidence contains no direct recipe-order manipulation, no matching assertion, and no connection from the reported reproducer to this specialized transform.
Causal confidence: 0.42
Build risk: New transformation code relies on a cast<VPWidenRecipe> when cloning the sinkable expression; the surrounding eligibility logic is only partially visible.; Regression coverage was updated for generic and AArch64 epilogue find-last cases, but not for the reported crash attachment.; 58 hunks were omitted from review, and the unavailable crash output prevents comparing the assertion site with this transform.

+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds double, ptr %src, i64 %iv
+  %val = load double, ptr %gep, align 8
+  %neg = fneg double %val
+  %c.1 = fcmp une double %neg, 10.0
+  br i1 %c.1, label %latch, label %early.exit

+latch:
+  %iv.next = add nuw i64 %iv, 1
+  %exit.cond = icmp eq i64 %iv.next, 127
+  br i1 %exit.cond, label %exit, label %loop.header
+
+early.exit:
+  ret i64 %iv
+
+exit:
+  ret i64 10
+}

Summary: This VPlan change teaches VPInstruction handling to recognize the called Function operand for both masked and unmasked call recipes, uses that result to compute call operand counts, and classifies calls as memory-reading/writing unless the called function is marked doesNotAccessMemory. It also adjusts dereferenceability analysis to stop at VPIRBasicBlock nodes and asserts if a non-load recipe unexpectedly reads memory; new LoopVectorize early-exit tests cover call- and unary-operation cases.

The accompanying tests retarget -vplan-print-after from the prior optimize-name regex to the new explicit pass name. The change is labeled NFC and the added hook body does not mutate the VPlan.

+; RUN: opt < %s -passes=loop-vectorize -disable-output -debug-only=loop-vectorize 2>&1 | FileCheck %s
+; REQUIRES: asserts
+target triple = "aarch64"
+
+; CHECK: Cost of 1 for VF 2: EMIT vp<{{.*}}> = first-order splice
+; CHECK: Cost of 3 for VF vscale x 2: EMIT vp<{{.*}}> = first-order splice
+
+define void @foo(ptr noalias %in, ptr noalias %out, i64 %n) "target-features"="+sve" {
+entry:
+  %load.prev = load i64, ptr %in, align 8
+  br label %for.body
+
+for.body:
+  %indvars.iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %indvars.iv.next, %for.body ]
+  %prev = phi i64 [ %load.prev, %entry ], [ %load.cur, %for.body ]
+  %indvars.iv.next = add nuw nsw i64 %indvars.iv, 1
+  %arrayidx.load = getelementptr inbounds nuw i64, ptr %in, i64 %indvars.iv.next
+  %load.cur = load i64, ptr %arrayidx.load
+  %add = add i64 %load.cur, %prev
+  %arrayidx.store = getelementptr inbounds nuw i64, ptr %out, i64 %indvars.iv
+  store i64 %add, ptr %arrayidx.store
+  %exitcond.not = icmp eq i64 %indvars.iv.next, %n
+  br i1 %exitcond.not, label %for.cond.cleanup, label %for.body, !llvm.loop !0
+
+for.cond.cleanup:
+  ret void
+}
+
+!0 = distinct !{!0, !1, !2}
+!1 = !{!"llvm.loop.mustprogress"}
+!2 = !{!"llvm.loop.unroll.disable"}

+

+entry:
+  %load.prev = load i64, ptr %in, align 8
+  br label %for.body
+

+  %indvars.iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %indvars.iv.next, %for.body ]
+  %prev = phi i64 [ %load.prev, %entry ], [ %load.cur, %for.body ]
+  %indvars.iv.next = add nuw nsw i64 %indvars.iv, 1
+  %arrayidx.load = getelementptr inbounds nuw i64, ptr %in, i64 %indvars.iv.next

+  %exitcond.not = icmp eq i64 %indvars.iv.next, %n

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends ConstantFolding::FoldBitCast to support byte-typed constants and vectors. It folds byte values through same-width integer vectors, adds poison-bit tracking and restoration for byte/vector conversions, and broadens scalar/vector constant handling to include ConstantByte.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/clang/test/Driver/linux-ld-args.c
@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+/// Tests that gnutools::Linker::ConstructJob forwards user command-line options
+/// to the ld invocation. Sysroot-dependent toolchain discovery and
+/// crt*/library-path selection live in linux-ld.c.
+
+/// Mixed -Xlinker, -Wl, and standalone forwarding. -T is reordered to the end
+/// so that earlier -L paths take precedence.
+// RUN: %clang --target=x86_64-linux-gnu -### \
+// RUN:   -e _start -T a.lds -t -Xlinker one -Xlinker --no-demangle \
+// RUN:   -Wl,two,--no-demangle,three -Xlinker four -z five -r %s 2>&1 | \
+// RUN:   FileCheck --check-prefix=MIXED %s
+// MIXED: "--no-demangle" "-e" "_start" "one" "two" "three" "four" "-z" "five" "-r" {{.*}} "-T" "a.lds" "-t"
+
+/// Passthrough flags. -rdynamic becomes -export-dynamic; -Wl,-z keyword pairs
+/// are forwarded as separate "-z" KEYWORD tokens.
+// RUN: %clang --target=x86_64-linux-gnu -### \
+// RUN:   -s -u my_sym -rdynamic -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now %s 2>&1 | \
+// RUN:   FileCheck --check-prefix=PASS %s
+// PASS:      "-s"
+// PASS-SAME: "-export-dynamic"
+// PASS-SAME: "-u" "my_sym"
+// PASS-SAME: "-z" "relro" "-z" "now"
+
+/// -nopie is OpenBSD-specific.
+// RUN: not %clang -### --target=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu %s -nopie 2>&1 | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=CHECK-NOPIE
+// CHECK-NOPIE: error: unsupported option '-nopie' for target 'x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu'
